claim: A private limited company is incorporated online through the MCA portal using the SPICe+ form (Part A reserves the name, Part B does incorporation, PAN, TAN, EPFO, ESIC and optionally GSTIN together). Every director needs a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC); DINs are allotted through the same form. MCA charges no incorporation fee for authorised capital up to ₹15 lakh, but state stamp duty on the MoA/AoA still applies and varies by state.
note: Fee waiver threshold and stamp duty should be re-verified against the current MCA fee rules.

claim: Name reservation is rejected for reasons that feel arbitrary: too similar to an existing company or trademark, a generic word, or a word that needs approval (Bank, Exchange, National...). Each resubmission burns days. Two names can be proposed per attempt.

sources.title: Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, rule 8; common founder complaints on forums

claim: After incorporation a company must file INC-20A (declaration of commencement of business) within 180 days, after the subscribers have paid for their shares into the company bank account. Missing it attracts penalties on the company and directors, and the company cannot borrow or start business until it is filed.
The board must appoint the first auditor within 30 days of incorporation. In practice the CA who incorporated you expects to be that auditor and prices the year accordingly.

Running a dormant-ish private limited company costs money every year regardless of revenue: statutory audit, AOC-4, MGT-7, ADT-1, DIR-3 KYC for each director, and income tax return. Typical CA retainer for a tiny company is ₹15,000–40,000 a year, more in metros.
note: Filing list is real; the fee range is an estimate from anecdotes and should be replaced with a sourced range.

claim: GST registration is mandatory for a service business once aggregate turnover crosses ₹20 lakh in a financial year (₹10 lakh in some special-category states). Below that it is voluntary. A registered B2B customer will still ask for a GST invoice so they can claim input tax credit; without a GSTIN you cannot issue one, and many procurement teams will not onboard an unregistered vendor at all.

sources.title: CGST Act 2017, s.22; s.24 for compulsory registration cases

claim: Once registered, GST returns are due every month (GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B) or quarterly under the QRMP scheme, even when there is nothing to report. Late fees accrue per day. Most founders hand this to a CA at ₹1,000–3,000 a month.

sources.title: CGST Rules; late fee under s.47

claim: When a company pays you for professional or technical services above the threshold, it deducts TDS under section 194J before paying (10% for professional fees, 2% for technical services). You receive less than you invoiced and get the rest back only when you file your income tax return, months later. First-time founders read this as the customer short-paying them.

Indian payment gateways onboard individuals and sole proprietors: a PAN, a bank account and basic KYC are enough to start accepting payments. You do not need a registered company. Many founders believe otherwise and stall the project on that belief.

sources.title: Razorpay / Cashfree onboarding documentation for individuals and proprietorships

note: KYC rules tighten periodically; re-verify what document set is currently accepted.

claim: Most Indian tech employment contracts include an IP assignment clause covering anything built during employment, sometimes regardless of whether company time or equipment was used, and a non-compete or moonlighting clause. Enforceability varies, but the clause is enough to scare an acquirer or investor during diligence.

sources.title: Standard Indian employment agreements; Indian Contract Act s.27 limits non-competes

claim: Small Indian agencies quote ₹2–8 lakh for a B2B SaaS MVP and 6–10 weeks. The quote is always confident. The delivered scope is decided by whoever wrote the SoW, which was you, badly.
note: Range and timelines are invented from anecdotes; replace with a sampled set of real quotes.

claim: Udyam (MSME) registration is free and online, needs only Aadhaar and PAN, and is worth having: some customers and banks ask for it, and it unlocks delayed-payment protection under the MSMED Act.
DPIIT Startup India recognition is free and mostly paperwork. It does not by itself give a tax holiday; that needs a separate Inter-Ministerial Board approval that most startups never get.
